findings.evidence: A change outside the listed deliverables widens the scope.

findings.summary: A request sentence that names the part and says 'later', 'out of scope' or 'for now' does not count as deferring it, so a reading that follows the request is refused; the plan also goes against criterion 4's 'later' example without saying so.
findings.evidence: Decision 7: a part is deferred only by a DEFER_PHRASES phrase, and 'Bare later, future, for now, separately, defer and out of scope do not defer a part', even in a sentence that names the marker. DEFER_PHRASES (Decision 6) has no 'later', 'out of scope' or 'for now'. Counterexamples: 'Part (3) is out of scope for now.' and 'Part 3 can come later.' leave part 3 required. The reader then cannot follow the request: out_of_scope never covers, and a criterion that defers is ignored. Accepted criterion 4 says the request defers a part with words 'for example 'later' or 'follow-up''. The demonstration only tests 'in a follow-up job' and 'can wait for a follow-up job'. The plan already trusts the broader MARKER_NEGATION list when a criterion names the marker, so the same reasoning applies to request sentences. Fix: For a request sentence outside every part that names the part's marker ((N), N), part N, item N, (c), part c), use MARKER_NEGATION (which includes later, out of scope, for now, defer, skip). Keep the narrow DEFER_PHRASES list only for unmarked text. Add Accept cases 'Part (3) is out of scope for now.' and 'Part 3 can come later.', and a unit test with 'later' that matches criterion 4's example. If bare 'later' inside the part's own text stays excluded, say so as a stated departure from criterion 4.
findings.location: Decision 7 (request-side deferral) and Demonstration for criterion 4

findings.summary: Alternatives and optional parts are treated as required parts. A reading that picks one option, as the request allows, is refused with no honest repair.
findings.evidence: Decision 3 reads any inline '(1)..(2)..' or '(a)..(b)..' sequence of at least 2 markers, and every line-start N./N)/(N)/a)/(a), as an Enumerated part, and Decision 5 requires each to be covered. Nothing looks at 'or', 'either', 'one of', 'choose', 'optionally' or 'if time permits'. Counterexample: 'Store it either as (a) a JSON file or (b) a TOML table.' A reading that chooses (a) is refused for (b). out_of_scope never covers, and the only repair is a criterion for work that will not be done. This is the kind of obvious false positive the soundness question asks about. Neither the corpus nor the proxy test has such a case. Fix: Treat an inline sequence whose last marker follows ' or ', or a list introduced by 'either', 'one of', 'choose' or 'pick', as one group that is covered when any member is covered. Treat a part whose text starts with 'optionally', or holds 'if time permits' or 'nice to have', as deferrable. Add corpus Accept cases for each, and pin the limit in the doc comment.
findings.location: Decision 3 (inline and line-start Enumerated parts) and Decision 5 (coverage)

findings.summary: The marker of a Bullet part is undefined, so it is unclear whether marker-cited coverage and MARKER_NEGATION apply to bullets.
findings.evidence: RequestPart {marker, kind, text} is defined for both kinds, but dash and star bullets have no marker. If the producer numbers bullets by position, the clause in this job's own criterion 2, 'leaves (3) out ... as a follow-up', would name bullet 3's marker and cancel the criterion under MARKER_NEGATION. That makes the own-reading Accept case depend on an unstated choice. Fix: State that Bullet parts have no marker (marker = None) and that rule 5(c) and the MARKER_NEGATION rules apply only to Enumerated parts. Numbered `N.` bullets inside the Acceptance section count as Bullet and get no marker either.
findings.location: Decision 1 (RequestPart.marker) and Decision 5(c) / Decision 6 marker rules

findings.summary: The timeout checks.rs is crates/athena-core/src/checks.rs, not reading/checks.rs. The plan names the wrong file and excuses 'checks.rs' in the diff check.
findings.evidence: Grep shows 54 timeout matches in crates/athena-core/src/checks.rs, 5 in run/checks.rs and none in reading/checks.rs. The plan's sza7 reading lists 'crates/athena-core/src/reading/checks.rs' as already landed or rejected and says 'git diff shows none of the listed timeout files touched except checks.rs (a stated deliverable)'. Fix: Name crates/athena-core/src/checks.rs in the sza7 fixture's out_of_scope, and have the diff check assert that it, display.rs, status_durations.rs, disk.rs, run/mod.rs and status.rs are untouched. reading/checks.rs is the deliverable and is a different file.
findings.location: Demonstration for criterion 6 (sza7 reading out_of_scope and git diff check)

findings.summary: A deliverable path alone covers a part. That contradicts the plan's own error text ('cover it with a deliverable and a criterion') and the first introspection's proposal, and generic path words can cover a dropped part.
findings.evidence: Rule (b): 'one deliverable path alone (split on non-alphanumerics) shares that many'. Paths in this repo all carry 'crates', 'core' and 'src', and test files carry 'tests' (stem 'test'). A part such as '(3) Add a core test for X' can be covered by crates/athena-core/tests/foo.rs with no criterion about it. Introspection 20261029-111106-c3pq asked for 'at least one deliverable and one acceptance criterion'. Fix: Either drop rule (b), or drop the path segments crates, src, core, tests, lib, mod and file extensions from path stems and reword the error to say 'a deliverable or a criterion'. Add a case where a test-file deliverable alone does not cover a dropped test part.
findings.location: Decision 5 rule (b) and the error text in step 4

findings.summary: Only a line equal to `Acceptance:` opens the bullet section, so hand-written headings such as 'Acceptance criteria:' or '## Acceptance' leave their bullets unenforced.
findings.evidence: Decision 3: 'A line equal (trimmed, case-insensitive) to `Acceptance:` opens the section.' Generated requests use exactly 'Acceptance:' (steward.rs:581, hestia), but users may write variants. This misses dropped parts rather than refusing good readings. Fix: Also accept 'Acceptance criteria:', '## Acceptance' and '## Acceptance criteria', or list the exact-heading limit in the doc comment next to the other known limits.

summary: Read: checks.rs:492-640, terms.rs:50-208, topics.rs:157-282, work_decisions.rs:175-349, replay.rs:130-308, refusal_corpus.rs:160-299, 1320-1400, 1870-1920, the step-order source tests in reading.rs, and CHANGELOG.md:1-14. The overall design holds: one shared filter for generated and copied text (`request_own_lines` factored out of `plain_request_prose`), the new step placed last in `refusing_check` so every existing refusal keeps its check, approved-work requests yielding no parts after `## Source`, and clear seams with demonstrations that fail without the step. The worked stem examples come out as stated. Two soundness problems remain, and each refuses a reading that follows the request faithfully with no honest repair. (1) The request-side deferral rule ignores "later", "out of scope" and "for now" even in a sentence that names the part's marker, which also contradicts accepted criterion 4's 'later' example. (2) Alternatives such as "(a) ... or (b) ..." and optional parts are all treated as required. Smaller issues: bullet markers are undefined; the sza7 fixture names the wrong checks.rs as a timeout file and excuses it in the diff check; a deliverable path alone can cover a part, against the plan's own error text; and only an exact `Acceptance:` heading is recognised.
